title: Zayd chooses
hook: Zayd, a freed boy in the house, chooses to stay with him rather than go home with his own father

segments.voice: Yesterday, their children: four daughters, and little sons who died, al-Qasim among them, whose name his father carried. Your line was: every child remembered. Whose name did you keep? Day seven hundred nineteen.

A father has been looking for his son for a long time. The boy was taken in a raid, the sirah says, and sold in a market far from home. The father mourned him in verse: I weep for Zayd, and I don't know what became of him. Then word comes. The boy is alive, in Mecca, in the house of a man of Quraysh, Muhammad ibn Abdullah. The father and his brother ride south with money to buy him back. They find him. And the boy says no. Today: Zayd chooses.
screen: `A BOY TAKEN IN A RAID.` → `A FATHER WEEPS IN VERSE.` → `THE BOY SAYS NO.`

segments.voice: Here's how the sirah tells it. Zayd ibn Harithah came into the house as a gift. Khadijah's nephew had bought him, she received him, and she gave him to her husband, the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. When Zayd's father, Harithah, arrived with the ransom, the Prophet didn't haggle. He said, in the account Ibn Sa'd keeps: call him, and let him choose. If he chooses you, he's yours, with no price. If he chooses me, I'm not a man to turn away someone who chooses me. So they called Zayd. Do you know these men? Yes, my father and my uncle. And Zayd said: I won't choose anyone over you. His father was stunned. You'd choose slavery over your own father and family? And Zayd answered that he had seen something in this man that he would never trade. Then the Prophet took him by the hand to the gathering place by the Ka'ba and said to the people: bear witness, Zayd is my son. And the father, the report says, went home at peace. After that, people called him Zayd ibn Muhammad. Sahih al-Bukhari records that they kept calling him that until a verse came, and Pickthall renders its opening: "Proclaim their real parentage." So he was Zayd ibn Harithah again, his own father's son. But the bond stayed. And the Qur'an itself, at surah thirty-three, verse thirty-seven, mentions Zayd by name. A boy who chose a house, kept in the Book.
screen: `A GIFT IN KHADIJAH'S HOUSE.` · `CALL HIM, AND LET HIM CHOOSE.` · `BEAR WITNESS, ZAYD IS MY SON.` · `HIS OWN FATHER'S NAME RESTORED.` · then, large: `HE CHOSE TO STAY.`

segments.voice: The practice: thank someone who chose you. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind a person who picked you when they didn't have to. A friend who stayed. A stepparent. A teacher who took a chance. A partner. Someone who let you choose, and then honored what you chose. Hold their face for a moment. What did it cost them to choose you? If you pray, you can thank Allah for them by name. If not, just let the gratitude sit in your chest a while. The bell holds the time.
Zayd chooses. Offered his freedom and his father's home, Zayd ibn Harithah chose to stay with the Prophet, who then called him his son. Today's word.
Your line: he chose to stay. Today, send one short message to someone who chose you, and tell them what it meant. Day seven hundred nineteen.

howItsDone: Muslims remember Zayd ibn Harithah as a beloved companion of the Prophet ﷺ, and his story is told when teaching about the Qur'an's ruling that adopted children keep their birth parents' names.

notes: The father's search, his verse of mourning, the choice and the declaration at the Ka'ba follow Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Hisham's notes; the dialogue is paraphrased. Confirm the sequence (freedom and adoption after the choice) and that 'the father went home at peace' is in the report.
Hook says 'taken in a raid' and 'sold in a market far from home' (the market at Ukaz in some reports); confirm.
Index hook calls Zayd 'a freed boy'; in the reports he is freed and adopted after his choice. Script follows the reports; suggest the index read 'a boy in the house'.
Pickthall 33:5 opening quoted from memory; confirm wording.
The later marriage of Zayd and Zaynab bint Jahsh (33:37) is not told here; only that the verse names him.
Editor: hook no longer says the father learned of 'a man called al-Amin' (the reports of the search don't use the title); it now names the house as that of Muhammad ibn Abdullah of Quraysh.
Audit: read in full; Ibn Sa'd sequence, Bukhari 4782 and the 33:5 / 33:37 references are consistent with the reports. No changes.
